title: Comparison, Choices & Envy
subtitle: Social media, social pressure and envy

scenario.title: The Comparison Illusion
scenario.text: An influencer posts beautiful photos of her home, dinners and weekends. Her followers assume her life is nearly perfect, but they don't see the staged photos, the money worries or the hard work behind the scenes.

scenario.title: Are You Choosing for Yourself?
scenario.text: Sarah has always liked a simple life. When her friends start buying luxury brands, she starts spending too — not because she wants to, but because she's afraid of looking less successful. Months later, she has less money and a lifestyle that doesn't suit her.

scenario.title: Is Envy Always a Bad Thing?
scenario.text: Envy can be destructive: you feel resentful and secretly hope others fail. But it can also be motivating: someone's success shows you what you want and pushes you to take action.

expressions.meaning: a version of your life that is selected and edited to look good.
expressions.example: Most profiles show a carefully curated image, not real life.

expressions.meaning: to believe something exactly as it looks, without questioning it.
expressions.example: Don't take every perfect post at face value.

expressions.meaning: to make you see things in a way that isn't accurate.
expressions.example: Constant scrolling can distort your perception of reality.

expressions.meaning: to do something because others expect it, not because you want to.
expressions.example: Sarah gave in to social pressure and bought things she didn't need.

expressions.meaning: to forget what really matters to you.
expressions.example: When you compare yourself all the time, you lose sight of your priorities.

expressions.meaning: to need approval from other people to feel good about yourself.
expressions.example: Posting every achievement can be a way to seek external validation.

expressions.en: measure success on your own terms
expressions.meaning: to judge success by your own values, not by other people's.
expressions.example: I prefer to measure success on my own terms.

expressions.meaning: to use the feeling of wanting what others have as a push to act.
expressions.example: She turned her envy into motivation and started a course.

expressions.meaning: to use someone's example to motivate you.
expressions.example: I take inspiration from people who changed careers later in life.

build.prompt: Why do the influencer's followers think her life is perfect?
build.explain: "The highlights" are the best moments. A "staged" photo is planned to look natural.

build.prompt: What is the main message of the first slide?
build.explain: "Curated" means carefully selected and organised, like the objects in a museum.

build.prompt: How do you react when you see a perfect post?
build.explain: "Take something at face value" means to accept it as true without questioning it. Remember: AT face value.

build.prompt: Can social media change how we see the world?
build.explain: "Distort" means to change something so it is no longer accurate. Notice: perception OF reality.

build.prompt: Why did Sarah change her lifestyle?
build.explain: "Fit in" means to feel accepted by a group.
"Give in to" means to stop resisting. "Lose sight of" means to forget what is really important.

build.prompt: Why do some people post every achievement?
build.explain: "External validation" is approval that comes from other people, not from yourself.
"On your own terms" means according to your own rules and values. Remember: based ON, not based in.
"Turn X into Y" means to transform X into Y. Envy helps when it pushes you to act.

build.prompt: How do confident people react to someone else's success?
build.explain: Notice the prepositions: threatened BY, inspiration FROM.

speak.question: Is presenting an idealized version of yourself online a form of dishonesty, or is it simply a matter of privacy?
speak.explain: "It depends on…" is a simple way to give a balanced opinion.

speak.question: Should people care about how others perceive their lifestyle, or should personal satisfaction come first? Defend your position.
speak.explain: "I'd argue that…" and "I'd rather…" make your position clear and polite.

speak.question: Imagine your friend gets an opportunity you've wanted for years. What would your first reaction be, and how would you handle it?
blocks: I'd feel a bit envious at first.
and try to turn that feeling
speak.explain: Use "would" ('d) to talk about imaginary situations: I'd feel, I'd congratulate.
